transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Yeah… so, what’s been bothering me is this thing at work, mostly. I work retail, and if I even think there might be a bat in the stockroom—or anything kind of flapping around back there—my body just reacts immediately. Like, before I can even talk myself down, my heart jumps hard, I start sweating, and I get this overwhelming feeling that I need to get out of there right then.

It’s not like I’m calmly deciding, “Oh, I don’t like this.” It’s more like my whole body hits the panic button the second the thought crosses my mind. That’s basically what brought me in.

Does this kind of strong physical reaction—like your heart jumping, sweating, and feeling like you need to escape—happen in other situations, or is it mostly when you're thinking about something flapping or possibly bats in the stockroom?

It’s mostly that kind of thing, yeah—anything that looks like it could be a bat, or even just a quick flutter in the back hallway. Like, I can tell you sitting here that I know a bat in the store probably isn’t going to hurt me. I know that logically. But in the moment, if I see something move fast near the ceiling or something dark kind of flap, my brain doesn’t treat it like “maybe that’s nothing.” It treats it like I’m in actual danger.

And it happens so fast that I don’t really get a chance to reason with myself first. It’s like my mind jumps straight to, “Get out, now.” So it’s not every stressful situation or anything like that—it’s really tied to that specific flapping, bat-looking kind of thing.
Have you ever experienced this kind of sudden panic or physical reaction in situations that don't involve bats or flapping things—like in crowded places, public transportation, or when you're alone?

No, not really in those kinds of situations. Like, I can be in a busy store or on a bus and I might be annoyed or uncomfortable, but it’s not that same immediate thing.

The reaction I’m talking about is really specific—like the second I think there might be a bat, or I see something that looks like it’s flapping around back in the stockroom, it just hits me. My heart jumps, I start sweating, and I get this really strong urge to get out of there right away. It feels almost automatic, like my body decides before I do.

So, crowded places or being alone don’t usually set it off like that. It’s that bat-or-flapping kind of situation that does it.
Do you find yourself avoiding going into the stockroom or certain parts of the store because of this fear of bats or flapping things?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I still go in when I absolutely have to because it’s my job, but I’ve definitely started working around it.

Like, I’ve been swapping out closing shifts when I can, because at night the back areas feel worse to me. And I’ll take the long way around the loading area instead of cutting through, even if it’s kind of ridiculous and takes extra time, because I just don’t want to deal with that feeling of maybe something being there.

And the stairwell is another one. If I have to check it, I’ll make myself do it, but I do it fast—like I’m kind of rushing through it—and I’m usually holding my phone the whole time like that somehow makes me safer. I know that probably sounds silly, but I feel scared the whole time I’m doing it. It’s not like I’m just casually walking through. I’m tense and trying to get it over with as quickly as possible.
